Yes. In the v2 snapshot, `heapq` exposes `heapify_max`, and it was added in Python 3.14.

```json
{"facts": {"available": "true", "added": "3.14"}}
```

`library/heapq.rst` documents `heapify_max(x)` under "For max-heaps, the following functions are provided". It describes the function as transforming list *x* into a max-heap in place, in linear time, and carries a `.. versionadded:: 3.14` note. The same page adds `heappush_max`, `heappop_max`, `heappushpop_max` and `heapreplace_max` in 3.14.

An earlier conversation note ("Max heaps") said `heapify_max` was absent. That note does not match this snapshot, so I relied on the corpus text.

Sources: `library/heapq.rst`
